# Discount Finder Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Discount Finder Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 5 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved procurement environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available and keep the workshop Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded sourcing knowledge, the proposed Dynamics 365 and Teams connections, and channel limits; document blocked paths instead of bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for each approved system and bind it only after security, privacy and business-owner review; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare procurement-manager, category-buyer, finance-director and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Discount, pricing-notice and demand-consolidation reviews by category, as tracked today Establish where signals, review deadlines and sourcing leverage are missed today before attributing change to the adapted agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Category | Supplier | Signal type | Review-by date | Evidence source | Facilities buying | Reviewer | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Procurement business owner | Approve source systems, review scope and success measures; keep commercial commitments behind approved procurement controls. |
| Authorized category manager | Own sourcing review and timing decisions through the approved procurement process. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any sourcing connection is approved. |
| Procurement connection owners | Approve customer systems after security, privacy and business-owner review; record identities and least-privilege references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check DISC-01 through DISC-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject evidence lacking its markers or Draft state. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route commercial decisions to the category manager. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed before production.
- [ ] The procurement owner records where discount terms, price notices and facility demand are tracked today before agreeing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/procurement-support/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The authentication option, required sign-in and allowed audience are approved for contract, forecast and pricing data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/procurement-support/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/procurement-support/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/procurement-support/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/procurement-support/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Discount Finder Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_procurement-support-rules-and-guardrails.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_procurement-support-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_consolidation-analysis_03
9. Add skill: aibast_purchase-timing_04
10. Add skill: aibast_savings-scan_01
11. Add skill: aibast_time-sensitive-deals_02
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass DISC-01: Procurement Manager
15. Pass DISC-02: Category Buyer
16. Pass DISC-03: Finance Director
17. Pass DISC-04: Category Buyer
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: DISC-01, DISC-02, DISC-03, DISC-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If Easy mode is chosen, the source-controlled project uses cli-copilot in the approved environment and stays Draft.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `ProcurementSupportAgent` and returns `DISC-101` and `DISC-102`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Case passes rest on the deterministic validator; an annotated image is a learner checkpoint, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing contract, pricing or demand data. Request only the scopes needed for approved read sources and review workflows. Restrict the allowed audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 — read:** Bind approved least-privilege read-only connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Recommend no award; list the consolidation tradeoffs for the authorized category manager. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a supplier contact, quote, order, renewal or commitment.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — read-write:** Gate any brief-sharing workflow behind approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Recommend no award; list the consolidation tradeoffs for the authorized category manager. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a sourcing-review brief for the authorized category manager and state that no commitment occurred.

### Step 3-3. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement connection owners

Create dedicated connection references only for approved systems and verify least-privilege access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Only customer-approved systems are bound after review; no supplier contact, quote, order or commitment is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Dedicated connection references exist only for approved systems, with least-privilege access verified.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended sourcing users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user connection access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The procurement owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic spend, gaps and dates are not acceptance thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations identify the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked sourcing corpus | All four cases, DISC-01 through DISC-04, return every required marker and avoid every forbidden phrase. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Commercial authority boundary | Any supplier selection or contact, quote, order, renewal, contract change or spend commitment is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved sourcing audience and supported channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review sourcing session transcripts, failed interactions, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
